text: Git branching is a key part of version control. When you work on a new feature, you create a feature branch. This keeps your changes separate from the main code, so the project stays stable. Once your work is finished, you can merge the branch back into the main branch. Before merging, many teams use pull requests. A pull request lets others review your code, discuss it, and suggest changes. This workflow helps teams catch mistakes early and work together smoothly. By using feature branches, merging, and pull requests, developers can manage their projects in an organised and safe way.
